targets.authors: Chandra, S., Srivastava, S. C., & Theng, Y.-L.
targets.title: Evaluating the role of trust in consumer adoption of mobile payment systems: An empirical analysis.
targets.evidence_quote:
This study is a conceptual replication of the Chandra, Srivastava, & Theng (2010) study on the
role of trust in adopting a unique type of technology.
targets.outcome_quote:
Results are largely consistent and comparable with that of the original model;
we also found that user trust plays a vital role in OSS adoption intention. However, two of the
hypotheses had significantly different results in our model when compared to the original—
specifically, perceived reputation did not have a significant impact on trust in the technology,
and trust had a more powerful effect on the perceived usefulness of the technology.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors report general consistency and two explicit differences from the original, including absent reputation effect and a trust-usefulness effect absent originally. Conclusion validates the model generally rather than declaring all replication findings confirmed.

reasoning: A new international survey conceptually retests the Chandra et al. model. Full preprint acquired including references and appendices. Its cover explicitly identifies the final published title, DOI and authors, matching publisher landing metadata; internal working title differs. Only one original is retested; other trust and technology-acceptance citations are background.
